# Tables and instructional blocks {#sec-components}

Technical books need more than prose, code, mathematics, and figures. This
chapter defines portable tables and a small family of semantic blocks for
notes, warnings, exercises, solutions, projects, and laboratory work. Their
labels and source order carry meaning even when a reader removes all color and
layout.

## Tables that explain data {#sec-component-tables}

A table needs a stable identifier, a concise caption, genuine column headers,
and an intentional reading direction. @tbl-measurement-plan is referenced
before it appears; its prose column is deliberately wider than its numeric
columns, and units live in the headers instead of being repeated in every cell.

| Stage | Nominal voltage (V) | Tolerance (%) | Reader action |
|:------|--------------------:|--------------:|:--------------|
| Sensor | 0.25 | 2.0 | Confirm the quiet-state value. |
| Gain | 2.50 | 1.0 | Record the value before limiting. |
| Output | 3.30 | 5.0 | Compare against the load requirement. |

: Measurement and acceptance plan {#tbl-measurement-plan tbl-colwidths="[24,22,18,36]"}

[Table note: tolerances are illustrative and do not replace a component data
sheet.]{.table-note}

Cells may contain restrained inline markup, including `code`, units, and a
short explanatory phrase. They must not contain paragraphs of narrative that
would be clearer as prose or a list.

### Multipage behavior {#sec-component-multipage-table}

The [ordered bench-test sequence](#test-sequence-table) is long enough to
exercise page breaking in compact print profiles. The header must repeat when
an engine divides the table; HTML and EPUB retain one semantic table that
readers can navigate by row and column. This long-table form is deliberately
unnumbered: current Typst output wraps a captioned cross-reference table in an
unbreakable figure. Numbered tables therefore must fit within one print page.

#### Bench-test sequence {#test-sequence-table .table-title}

| Step | Operation | Expected evidence |
|----:|:----------|:------------------|
| 1 | Inspect the unpowered assembly. | Orientation marks agree with the drawing. |
| 2 | Confirm instrument range. | The selected range exceeds the expected input. |
| 3 | Attach the reference lead. | The reference node remains mechanically secure. |
| 4 | Apply current-limited power. | The supply remains below the configured limit. |
| 5 | Measure the input node. | The value falls inside the input tolerance. |
| 6 | Measure the conditioned node. | Gain agrees with the calculated interval. |
| 7 | Exercise the low boundary. | The output reports the low state once. |
| 8 | Return to the nominal input. | The output returns without oscillation. |
| 9 | Exercise the high boundary. | The output reports the high state once. |
| 10 | Repeat the nominal reading. | Drift remains within the stated allowance. |
| 11 | Remove the simulated input. | The defined idle state appears. |
| 12 | Restore the simulated input. | Normal operation resumes without a reset. |
| 13 | Record ambient conditions. | Temperature and supply voltage are present. |
| 14 | Capture the final waveform. | The trace includes scale and channel labels. |
| 15 | Compare against acceptance limits. | Every observation has a pass or fail result. |
| 16 | Save the raw observations. | The source record has a durable filename. |
| 17 | Remove power. | The supply reads zero before leads are moved. |
| 18 | Disconnect the fixture. | The work area returns to a safe state. |
| 19 | Inspect leads and connectors. | No conductor is loose, warm, or visibly damaged. |
| 20 | Archive the final settings. | Instrument ranges and limits accompany the readings. |
| 21 | Sign the observation record. | The operator and review date are identifiable. |
| 22 | Store reusable fixtures. | Protective covers and labels remain attached. |
| 23 | Record unresolved anomalies. | Each anomaly has an owner and next action. |
| 24 | Close the test session. | Raw evidence remains separate from interpretation. |

: {tbl-colwidths="[14,34,52]"}

[Table note: preserve the authored row order; it is also the required execution
order.]{.table-note}

## Notes, callouts, and warnings {#sec-component-callouts}

Callouts interrupt the normal reading rhythm, so authors use them only when a
reader benefits from a distinct decision, reminder, or hazard. The visible
title is mandatory; color and a future icon may reinforce the category but
never define it.

::: {#nte-measure-twice .callout-note .margin-note appearance="simple" icon=false}
## Margin note: measure twice

Record the instrument range with the reading. A value without its range can
hide clipping or insufficient resolution.
:::

@nte-measure-twice remains next to this discussion on a roomy web page. EPUB
and compact print profiles keep it inline at the same source position rather
than squeezing it into an unreadable physical margin.

::: {#tip-checkpoint .callout-tip appearance="simple" icon=false}
## Checkpoint before continuing

State what has been established and what the next section assumes. A checkpoint
is guidance, not a prerequisite hidden from the surrounding prose.
:::

::: {#wrn-disconnect-power .callout-warning appearance="simple" icon=false}
## Disconnect power before changing leads

De-energize the fixture, verify the supply reads zero, and discharge stored
energy before moving a connection. The imperative title and complete text carry
the hazard without relying on color.
:::

The procedure must obey @wrn-disconnect-power wherever a lead change could
expose stored energy.

## Exercises and solutions {#sec-component-exercises}

Exercises and solutions use Quarto's numbered theorem-family identifiers. The
generated label makes @exr-divider-budget durable even when chapters are
reordered; its solution carries the paired `sol-divider-budget` identifier. A
named solution may be placed immediately after its exercise in a teaching
edition or collected later without changing either identifier.

::: {#exr-divider-budget}
## Divider power budget

A 12 V source drives two series resistors, $R_1 = 2\,\mathrm{k}\Omega$ and
$R_2 = 4\,\mathrm{k}\Omega$. Calculate the current, the voltage across each
resistor, and the power dissipated by each resistor. State a suitable minimum
power rating using a safety factor of two.
:::

::: {#sol-divider-budget}
## Divider power budget

The series resistance is $6\,\mathrm{k}\Omega$, so the current is
$I = 12\,\mathrm{V}/6\,\mathrm{k}\Omega = 2\,\mathrm{mA}$. Therefore
$V_1 = 4\,\mathrm{V}$ and $V_2 = 8\,\mathrm{V}$. The dissipations are
$P_1 = I^2R_1 = 8\,\mathrm{mW}$ and $P_2 = I^2R_2 = 16\,\mathrm{mW}$;
doubling either value still fits comfortably within a 0.125 W rating.
:::

## Project and laboratory blocks {#sec-component-projects}

A project defines an outcome and constraints; a laboratory block defines a
repeatable procedure, evidence, and safety boundary. Neither is merely a long
warning or an exercise with extra prose.

::: {#project-threshold-indicator .project-anchor}
::: {.callout-note .project-block appearance="simple" icon=false}
## Project: build a threshold indicator

**Outcome.** Build a circuit that illuminates an indicator when a sensor signal
crosses an adjustable threshold.

**Constraints.** Use a current-limited supply, expose a labeled test point for
the sensor signal, and make the threshold adjustable over the documented input
range.

**Deliverables.** Provide a schematic, bill of materials, measured threshold,
and a short comparison between predicted and observed behavior.
:::
:::

::: {#lab-verify-threshold .lab-anchor}
::: {.callout-tip .lab-block appearance="simple" icon=false}
## Lab: verify the threshold indicator

**Before starting.** Read @wrn-disconnect-power and confirm the supply current
limit.

1. Set the input below the predicted threshold and record the output.
2. Increase the input slowly until the indicator changes state.
3. Repeat while decreasing the input to reveal any hysteresis.
4. Save the raw readings and ambient conditions.

**Evidence.** Submit the completed @tbl-measurement-plan fields, the two measured
transition points, and a conclusion that distinguishes observation from
inference.
:::
:::

## Authoring boundary {#sec-component-boundary}

Use a table only for genuinely tabular relationships. Use ordinary prose for
the main argument, a note for optional context, a warning for a hazard, an
exercise for a bounded reader task, a solution for its worked resolution, a
project for an outcome, and a lab for an evidence-producing procedure. Authors
must not imitate these components with bold paragraphs, manually typed numbers,
raw HTML, raw Typst, or raw LaTeX.
